title: #jajasafricanhairbraiding #jajabroadway #jocelynbioh #harlem #mtc #ny...
transcript: Yesterday my friend Kate and I saw Jaja's African Hair braiding on Broadway a world premiere new play following a group of women at a hair braiding salon in Harlem. It was a really enjoyable piece and it closes on November 19th so you have to go soon. Playwright Jocelyn Bioh describes the play as a love letter to the women owning and running these braiding shops that are huge part of the Harlem economy and culture. in the play we get a look into Jaja’s shop over the course of a given day and we see different kinds of customers coming in the everyday gossip and drama among the women working there and it's so impressive how captivating the show is despite it being basically just a day in the life kind of thing. I think that speaks to the tight pacing, direction and performances. It was really funny and really easy to be invested in all the characters. In a talkback following the performance I attended many Black audience members praised the specificity and the authenticity of the text and expressed how much they appreciated that this piece spotlights such a huge part of their culture and their stories. Someone noted that it's especially exciting to see given that in a lot of theatrical settings, Black hair isn't prioritized in terms of time, resources and attention paid. So for multiple reasons, this has definitely been a theatrical highlight of the fall Broadway season so far. With that, another Playbill for my collection
